import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 281

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/281](https://www.erdosproblems.com/281)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta
  Arithmetica (1936), 147-151.
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace Erdos281

/-- Choices of congruence classes $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def ResidueChoice (n : ℕ → ℕ) := ∀ i : ℕ, ZMod (n i)

/-- The integers avoiding all congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidAll (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/-- The integers avoiding the first $k$ congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidPrefix (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) (k : ℕ) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, i < k → (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos281.lean"]
theorem erdos_281 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε := by
  sorry

end Erdos281

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses two-sided natural density on ℤ, whereas the usual number-theoretic convention counts positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write A(a) for the infinite avoidance set and P_a(N) for its number of elements in [1,N]. Reflection gives A(-a) = -A(a), so |A(a) ∩ [-N,N]| = P_a(N) + P_{-a}(N) + 1_{0∈A(a)}. Consequently, positive-integer density zero for every residue choice implies two-sided density zero for every choice. Conversely, P_a(N) is bounded by the symmetric count, so symmetric density zero implies positive-integer density zero. Thus the universally quantified hypotheses are equivalent. Each finite-prefix avoidance set is periodic with positive period lcm(n(0),…,n(k−1)), and its positive-integer and two-sided densities both equal the fraction of avoiding residues in one period. The conclusions are therefore equivalent as well.

reformulations.difference: The finite-prefix conclusion quantifies over entire infinite residue sequences rather than just the first k residue choices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: avoidPrefix depends only on coordinates i < k. Every finite choice extends to an infinite choice by assigning zero outside the prefix, and every infinite choice restricts to a finite one. In scratch.lean, finite_choice_quantifiers_checked proves the corresponding ↔ for an arbitrary predicate on the avoidance set, which specializes to the density condition in this theorem.
